title: Army band background for jazz playing
summary: He explains that the National Guard concert band gave him the classical foundation behind his jazz playing.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: You, you love the whole -- all of the music. There was no particular facet of it, or instrumentalists that you liked? I mean, you were playing a lot of brass instruments like the French -- the trumpet. You were playing it before the trombone and the French horn. You'd studied those. But did you like -- did you have an especial liking for the trumpets, what they were doing, or maybe the trombones or the piano or just the full sound of an orchestra?

Yes. At that at that time I was with that, still with that army band, the National Guard. And my whole, my whole life in music revolved on that, in that, in that concert band, and, besides, that's where I learned the root of myself. In order to play jazz, you have to have the fund of background, and I think that was my background by the classic music that we rehearsed with the army band there,
and in between, and listening to the jazz bands around Chicago. That's what brings your embouchure and musical ability and everything pertaining to music....

An awful lot has been made about jazz rhyhtms and the beat in jazz, etc. There's always a discussion of the rhythm (Pause) Okay, did you...did those rhythms, how similar to the tribal songs and the tribal dance rhythms did you find jazz rhythms to be? Did you find any similarity or did you find a great deal of difference? Or did you have any difficulty making the adjustment or was it something that you just loved and gravitated toward?
